resources.string: Save an explicit “recognized text → correct text” pair, then choose Context-aware or Always replace for each entry.
Context-aware sends only the word pair and nearby text to the current language model so it can decide whether to apply the entry. The model cannot rewrite anything else.
Always replace runs entirely on device. Both modes affect only future transcripts and never change original model output or existing content.
“%1$s” → “%2$s”\n\nFuture replacements will stop. Completed transcripts and original model output will not change.
Choose contextual evaluation or local replacement for your word pairs
For example, when “Murmur note” is recognized, use context to decide whether it should become “Murmurnote.”
Waiting for a language-model API key; safely skipped for now
Nearby context will be evaluated when this matches
Exact matching text will be replaced on device
Both fields must contain 2–32 characters. Only text that exactly matches “Recognized as” can trigger this entry.
The entry itself will be enabled after saving; the master switch in Experimental features will remain off.
Recommended. Sends the word pair and nearby text, allowing the language model only to apply or keep it.
Recommended. No language-model API is configured, so the entry will be safely skipped until one is added.
Replaces exact matches locally without context. Use only for fixed terms that cannot be ambiguous.
The language model carefully evaluates nearby text
Replace exact matches without evaluating context
The context-aware entry limit (%1$d) has been reached. Disable one first, or change one to Always replace.
